newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House okays $4.1 bln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House okays $4.1 bln in bonds.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives after almost two hours of debate approved Wednesday by voice vote $4.1 billion in bond issues, State House News Service reported.

The approved measures included nearly $3.7 billion in funding for transportation projects statewide including Massachusetts's share of the $10.7 billion Central Artery/Third Harbor Tunnel Crossing project.

The measure authorizes Gov. William Weld's administration to borrow $1.2 billion for the Central Artery project, the nation's most expensive public construction project, in anticipation of future federal transportation grants -- something of a gamble.
But, as passed, the amount of those Grant Anticipation Notes is limited to $450 million.
Washington decides later this year how much will be allotted under the next round of transportation aid to the states.

The transportation bond totals $3.869 billion and covers two year's worth of transportation spending. It authorizes more than $2 billion for the Central Artery project; $750 million from the state's accounts for roads and bridges; and $504 million more in road and bridge work statewide that is reimbursable by the federal government.

The full House also approved a bill providing $200 million for the redevelopment of Fort Devens. The Fort Devens bill would provide the cash necessary to turn the closed Army base into a multipurpose transportation and industrial center.
Both measures must now go before the Senate for a vote.
